compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: The sailors reluctantly throw Jonah into the sea at his instruction, the storm stops, and they fear the LORD, offer a sacrifice, and make vows.
observations.label: Sailors sacrifice after the sea becomes calm

observations.body: The passage presents storm, reluctant action, prayer against guilt, calm, fear, sacrifice, and vows as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: storm, reluctant action, prayer against guilt, calm, fear, sacrifice, and vows

observations.body: The passage places outsider sacrifice beside storm, reluctant action, prayer against guilt, calm, fear, sacrifice, and vows.
observations.label: outsider sacrifice

payload.posture: Read Jonah 1:11–16 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the sacrifice follows deliverance and does not make throwing Jonah overboard a ritual offering
payload.title: Sailors sacrifice after the sea becomes calm
